items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: George Baquet was a very famous clarinet player who played in the twenties and the thirties, in fact he was one of the teachers of a great saxophone player and a clarinet player from New Orleans called Sidney Bechet. So my great uncle.

ctx.x: Right. Well they encouraged me in the way that they presented me the home that I grew up with with all of that. Because my father was a visual artist as well and my uncles were visual artists. So I had all that around me. I was seeing that, I was into music, seeing all the drawings and the paintings and stuff. So it was there. It was just like saying if you want it there it is. You make a choice, do I want to do this. I wasn’t forced. I got my first trumpet when I was nine. And in New Orleans with the shotgun…

was Baquet which is a French name — B-A-Q-U-E-T — George Baquet was a very famous clarinet player who played in the twenties and the thirties, in fact he was one of the teachers of a great saxophone player and a clarinet player from New Orleans called Sidney Bechet. So my great uncle.
I’ll be darned. That was your great uncle.
